comment: What the theme's roles look like with no package involved, and what was decided about each finding.
Collected by tools/review/roles-theme.mjs from the scss sources and the built bundle; the package's
Exact equality, not a ratchet down: a new finding and a resolved one both fail, because both are a
decision somebody has to record. Bank a new row by pasting it from the failure and filling in the
decision - a banked entry without one fails too.
slotLies - the slot word contradicts the CSS property the bundle shows it painting. Same rules as
above: banked with a decision, exact equality. hairline and rule-5 are deliberate and stay; naming
is a rename waiting for a changelog, not a role defect.
familyMismatches - a role from another family than the slot wants. Rows decided confirmed, rule-5
or package-gap came from the package audit (roles.decisions.json, open), with its vocabulary.
ladders - a slot whose states resolve to one role. `focused` reusing `hovered` is accepted
convention and never listed. decision no-rung means the system has no role for the second state
either; design means it does and we skip it.
concepts - one anatomical concept (modifiers + slot + state, sub-elements dropped) painted with
several roles across components. This is the only check that asks the question the task is named
after; every other one reads a single declaration. decision spelling means the roles resolve to one
colour and differ only in family, shade means same family different value, design means the
components disagree about the colour itself.

slotLies.name: color-view-border
slotLies.why: A border role drawn with background-color or box-shadow because the line is a 1px pseudo-element, not a real border. Name and role both say border; only the CSS property differs, and the package agrees (a separator is border-subtle). Re-checked 09.09.

slotLies.name: color-view-border-disabled
slotLies.why: A border role drawn with background-color or box-shadow because the line is a 1px pseudo-element, not a real border. Name and role both say border; only the CSS property differs, and the package agrees (a separator is border-subtle). Re-checked 09.09.

slotLies.name: diagram-selection-bg
slotLies.why: The name is right - fill on an SVG rect IS a background - and the role divergence is already recorded in DIVERGENCES.md. Re-checked 09.09.

slotLies.name: gantt-content
slotLies.why: Re-classified 09.09, and this one turned out to be correct. Every use is a drawn foreground mark, not a container: the milestone diamond as a box background, the dependency lines as 1px hairlines, the arrowhead as a border triangle. content is the right role for a mark and the right word for the name; the four CSS properties are just how CSS draws marks. This was sitting under rule-5, which claimed the name picked the dominant of two painted families - it does not, and it does not need to.

slotLies.name: grid-content-focused
slotLies.why: the focused cell's inner ring is drawn with outline-color in content-inverted - a white hairline inside the blue frame. The slot word follows the property, the role follows what the element is. It became visible to the scan only when D23 gave the paint a tier name; no pixel moved

concepts.why:
Answered 15.09 by validation, and the answer went against the guess. The three members are three unrelated things sharing the word accent: diagram paints stroke on .dxdi-spinner path - a SPINNER ARC; gantt paints border-color on a real border; scheduler paints the week-boundary grid line, which D19 already accepted as deliberately equal to the ordinary line.
The diagram member keeps content-primary, and that is not a preference: our own loadIndicator spinner sits on the identical role, and Blazor confirms it (loading-panel-indicator-no-area-indicator-color = content-primary). Moving it to border-primary, as the group name suggests, would drop the arc from 5.38 to 2.68 in light - under the 3:1 a graphic needs - because border-primary is the pale primary-70 outlier of its family. Same verdict as gantt-content: a drawn mark, painted by whatever property draws it, with a content role that is right.

Answered 15.09 by validation, confirmed as the reading proposed. Three members, three correct roles: list-base-select-all-separator-bg paints background-color with border-subtle, which is the hairline idiom and exactly what the package calls separator.color; scheduler-appointment-base-bg is the appointment fill on bg-primary-subtle, the role Blazor gives the same element; stepper-step-base-bg is a plain surface on bg. The word base means a different thing in each, which is what made them one group. Nothing to change.

grouped by the slot word, not by the element: the check box's -checked-bg IS a fill (checkbox.color.checked.default.bg.* = bg-primary*) and the radio's -checked-bg is the DOT, which the package models as an icon (radio-button.color.checked.icon.* = content-primary-shared*, with checked.bg.rest = color.none). Two families here is the anatomy being right, not a disagreement - and the values coincide anyway, primary-shared being one colour across families. Opened by D21

Answered 09.09, and the answer is not to unify. Measured: the whole *-danger-shared family resolves to ONE value across bg, border and content in both modes - that is what shared means in this set. So the family segment carries no colour information here; it records which property paints the value. The canonical spelling is therefore already decided by the theme's own slot rule (NAMING M3, family follows the painted property), and unifying the three would throw away the only information the segment carries. If the package ever diverges the three, each element will then correctly follow its own family - which is the outcome the original worry asked for. Every member of the cluster already obeys the rule: checkBox border paints border-color, checkBox fill paints background-color, checkBox mark is a glyph, common badge is a fill. The one exception is radioButton, which paints a border AND a fill from a single variable - that is not a spelling choice, it is the anatomy question filed as sweep:radio-invalid-vs-checkbox-invalid. All three roles here resolve to one colour (#76000b light / #9d0013 dark), so this row is a pure spelling cluster and nothing else.
